findings.title: Reschedule cleanup uses forEach(async) and never finishes
findings.body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the calendar/video cleanup at line 125 was switched to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await the now-async getCalendar. Array.forEach does not wait for async callbacks and drops their return values, so the try/catch around it never sees failures, and Reschedule still sends the reschedule email and returns true while deletion is in flight. This is a regression from the async app-store change: previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least invoked before the callback yielded, and deleteMeeting started the provider call before returning. Now the calendar path awaits getCalendar before deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting (videoClient.ts) awaits getVideoAdapters before calling the provider, and nothing awaits either promise. The old event can remain on the external calendar and the video meeting can stay up; on serverless the runtime often freezes that work after the handler returns, so the cleanup never runs. Replace forEach with for...of or Promise.all and await both getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside the try.

findings.title: Wipe-my-cal reschedule never awaits event deletion
findings.body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts the cleanup that is supposed to remove the previous calendar event and video meeting (line 125) uses forEach with an async callback and awaits getCalendar inside it. forEach ignores that promise, so the try/catch does not handle rejections, and the function sends the reschedule email and returns true without waiting. Making getCalendar and deleteMeeting async makes this worse than the old fire-and-forget: both now yield before the provider call (getCalendar before deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting before videoAdapter.deleteMeeting), and those promises are discarded. Wipe My Cal's reschedule path can therefore leave the previous event on the external calendar, so the slot stays busy and the app fails at the thing it exists to do. Use for...of or Promise.all and await getCalendar, deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting before returning.

findings.title: Request-reschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
findings.body: In the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, the booking is already written as CANCELLED (around line 475) and then bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) at line 553 awaits getCalendar and returns calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting. forEach does not await those callbacks, and this mutation has no try/catch around them, so a failure becomes an unhandled rejection rather than a failed mutation. The handler then awaits sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks and resolves successfully while external cleanup may not have started. getCalendar and deleteMeeting are now async and both yield before the provider request, so discarding the callback promise means the Google/Outlook event and the video meeting are often never deleted (especially once a serverless response is sent and pending work is frozen). Attendees are told to reschedule and the slot can be double-booked or left blocked on the calendar. Collect the work with Promise.all or for...of and await deleteEvent and deleteMeeting before sending email or webhooks.

findings.title: Cancelling remaining recurring bookings drops calendar deletes
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, when all remaining instances of a recurring booking are cancelled, external calendar deletion is done with credentials.forEach(async ...) at line 460, and this PR added await getCalendar as the first line of that callback. forEach does not wait for the async callback, and apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) runs only after await calendar.deleteEvent, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) (line 652) does not include these deletes and cannot observe their errors. Because getCalendar is now async, the callback yields before deleteEvent is even called; previously getCalendar was sync so the provider delete was at least started. The handler still marks the bookings CANCELLED and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." The non-recurring branch just below (line 480) was correctly rewritten to for...of and pushes the delete promise onto apiDeletes; the recurring branch needs the same treatment (push calendar.deleteEvent(...) without awaiting it inside an abandoned forEach, or await a Promise.all of those calls) or cancelling a series leaves every occurrence on the external calendar.

findings.title: Top-level import() preloads every app and can crash on a failed one
findings.body: packages/app-store/index.ts builds appStore with bare import() calls (applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), and the same for every other integration starting at line 3). Those expressions run as soon as the module is evaluated, not when a key is used, so the first import of appStore — which booking, calendar, video, and payment code all do — starts loading every integration package even if the request needs only one. Cold start and memory do not improve versus the old static imports, and every app module's top-level side effects still run on unrelated requests. A rejected import is also unhandled unless that specific key is later awaited. On Node 15+ the default is to terminate the process on an unhandled rejection, so one broken unused app can crash the server during an unrelated booking. Store thunks (() => import("./applecalendar")) and call them at the existing await sites so only the requested app loads and the caller can catch a failure.
